reason: I re-underwrote every leg this week and the tape confirmed the book rather than challenged it, so paying real frictions to rearrange a thesis that is working would be churn dressed up as activity. The mandate is to own the physical refining-and-logistics margin of the Iran-war fuel crisis, and that margin is not merely intact, it is at record width: the US diesel crack broke $100 for the first time in August and printed above $106 in September, gasoline cracks are above $50, distillate inventories sit ~14% below the five-year seasonal average at the lowest seasonal level on record, refinery utilization is running 97.2% against a ~90% norm, and US jet fuel supply is the tightest in sixty-plus years. Goldman carries $63/bbl US diesel refining profit into 2027, so this is priced as a regime rather than a spike. My four refiners (MPC 20, VLO 18, PSX 10, PBF 7) and STNG at 14 are the physical expression of exactly that, and STNG's own Q3 disclosure -- LR2s at $64,900/day, MRs at $30,000/day, plus three-year charter-outs locked at $40,188 and $42,500/day -- shows the logistics leg is converting spot tightness into multi-year cash, not just headline beta. The 1.5%-ish mark-to-market loss on this leg since the 2026-09-21 fill is not thesis damage. The reporting is explicit that MPC's 5.3% drop on entry day was a sector-wide pullback with no company-specific news, driven by profit-taking after a run that has MPC and VLO up roughly 100-143% year to date, and Goldman raised its MPC objective from $376 to $472 on that very day. Selling a confirmed thesis into someone else's profit-taking is the specific mistake this book exists to avoid, and holding means my cost basis sits below where I would have to re-enter on 2026-09-30. The single named risk to this book was a Hormuz reopening, and that risk resolved in my favour inside the mark window rather than against me. Iran's 22 September offer to reopen the strait within seven days is what knocked STNG down 2.6%, and by 28 September Trump had rejected that conditional offer outright and told aides he expects strikes to resume after the November midterms, with Brent settling around $105 and vessel traffic through Hormuz still collapsed ~95%. The one genuine supply improvement, Saudi Arabia restoring its East-West pipeline to about 3.5m b/d, is if anything constructive for me: it delivers crude to refiners while doing nothing about the product and refining bottleneck that the crack spread actually prices. My two shorts are the same trade from the victim side and both remain correct on the evidence. Jet fuel at $4.55-$4.75 a gallon has doubled since January, the industry is absorbing $100bn more in fuel cost this year with net profit halving from $45bn to $23bn, and carriers are grounding aircraft and cutting routes, which is why JETS is +1.79% for me. On XRT, the Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% in a unanimous September vote with 16 of 18 officials projecting at least one more hike, against core PCE above 3% all year, so a squeezed consumer facing record diesel and pump prices is exactly the right thing to be short even though the leg is flat at +0.01% so far. Positioning also argues for patience over action. Every stop is intact and none is close to firing: the worst leg, STNG, is -3.50% against a -14% stop, and MPC is -3.22% against -13%. The calendar in front of me is a reason to be holding the position rather than assembling it, with Valero reporting Q3 on 22 October and Marathon on 3 November straight into record realised cracks, after the three majors already posted $12.6bn combined in the prior quarter. I am deliberately keeping the 14% cash rather than spending it. This is a single-factor book by design -- every long and both shorts win on expensive fuel and lose together on a genuine peace -- so with Iran actively floating offers, that cash at 4% is the only real ballast against the one headline that breaks the whole thesis at once, and it is worth more as insurance than as another 14% of refining beta. Nothing I learned this week improves on the current allocation, so the correct action is to take none.
